h1: Saphir hops for a soft citrus note in a pilsner
title: Saphir Hops for Soft Citrus in a Pilsner | Craft Beer School
desc: What Saphir hops bring to a Pilsner, where to add them for soft tangerine and floral notes plus how they compare with classic German aroma hops.
teaser: Saphir adds a gentle tangerine note to a German lager without making it taste like an IPA.
standfirst: Saphir is a German aroma hop with a soft citrus edge that classic noble varieties do not have. Used late and lightly, it gives a Pilsner a little lift without leaving the style behind.
sections: Saphir is a German aroma hop with a citrus accent

Saphir was released by the Hüll hop research centre in Bavaria in 2002, bred from Hallertau aroma lines. The aim was a variety with the elegant character of the old Hallertau landrace on a healthier plant.

It came out slightly different, in a useful way. Alpha acid is low, typically 2 to 4.5%. The aroma is floral and lightly spicy like its relatives, with a soft tangerine and sweet citrus note on top. That note is the reason to buy it. In a German lager it reads as freshness rather than fruit.
Where the citrus survives and where it does not

Hop aroma comes from volatile oils. Boiling drives most of them off. A Saphir addition at 60 minutes gives bitterness and almost no citrus. An addition at 10 minutes keeps some. A whirlpool addition after flame out, with the wort held near 80 °C for 20 to 30 minutes, keeps more, because the oils dissolve without boiling away as fast.

In practice that means Saphir is wasted as a bittering hop. Its alpha is too low to be economical and the character you paid for disappears. Let a clean bittering hop carry the IBU and save Saphir for the end.
A Pilsner schedule that lets Saphir speak

For a 1,000 litre German pils at 32 IBU, one workable pattern is:

  • Bitter to about 26 IBU at 60 minutes with a clean hop such as Magnum or Perle.
  • Add Saphir at 10 minutes for 4 to 5 IBU, around 1 g per litre at 3.5% alpha.
  • Add another 1 to 1.5 g per litre of Saphir to the whirlpool at about 80 °C.

That gives a beer that still reads as a crisp German pils, with a floral and tangerine top note the drinker notices on the second sip rather than the first. A German pils sits in a broad 22 to 40 IBU band, so you can move the bittering charge without breaking the style.
Dry hopping a lager with Saphir

Some brewers dry hop a pils lightly, around 1 to 2 g per litre, to push the citrus further. That moves the beer towards a modern hoppy lager. It works, but it changes the brief. Dry hop matter also brings grassy notes and haze. Cold lager temperatures slow extraction, so give it three to four days and keep oxygen out during the addition.

If you are brewing a classic pils, we would stop at the whirlpool. If you are brewing an Italian style pils or a hoppy lager, a light Saphir dry hop is a good place to start. Our guide to brewing a hoppy lager shows where that style draws its lines.
How Saphir compares with other soft hops

Against Hallertau Mittelfrüh, Saphir has more citrus and a little less spice. Against Liberty, an American variety from Hallertau lineage, it is more floral and less peppery. Against modern fruit hops, it is restrained, which is the point. A drinker should not be able to name the fruit, only say the beer smells bright.

Getting that restraint right batch after batch depends on understanding where hop oils go in your own kit. Whirlpool temperature, rest time and how quickly you cool all change the result.

A common mistake is to treat whirlpool and late additions as aroma only. They are not. Alpha acids keep isomerising as long as the wort is hot, more slowly below boiling but not at zero. A large Saphir whirlpool at 80 °C for half an hour can add a few IBU. In a pils every few IBU are noticeable.

Brewing software estimates whirlpool bitterness in different ways and none of them knows how fast your kit cools. The practical fix is to send a sample of the finished beer for an IBU test once, compare it with your calculation and then adjust your own late addition figure. After that, trim the 60 minute charge if the beer lands high.
Low alpha aroma hops in Indian storage

Saphir is bought for its oil. The oil goes first when hops are stored warm. Keep foils frozen at around minus 18 °C, buy what you will finish within a season and never leave an open bag in the brewhouse during the brew. In a hot month that alone can dull the citrus you are paying for.

Split your next pils at the whirlpool if your kit allows it, or brew two small pilot batches. Use your usual aroma hop in one and Saphir at the same weight in the other. Keep everything else identical. Taste them blind with two colleagues after lagering. If nobody can pick the Saphir beer, raise the whirlpool dose by half a gram per litre and try again.
faqs: Saphir is floral and lightly spicy with a soft tangerine and sweet citrus note. In a lager it reads as freshness rather than obvious fruit.
What is the alpha acid of Saphir hops?
Saphir usually measures 2 to 4.5% alpha acid, which makes it an aroma hop rather than a bittering one.
When should I add Saphir to a Pilsner?
Late: at 10 minutes, in the whirlpool near 80 °C or as a light dry hop. A 60 minute addition loses most of its citrus character.
